import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Convergence of fraction numerators $a(n)/b(n)$ to $e$

a: Numerators of a sequence of fractions converging to $e$.
$$a(1) = 3, a(2) = 5$$
For $n > 2$:
$$a(n) = \begin{cases} \left(\frac{n+2}{2}\right) a(n-1) - a(n-2) -
\left(\frac{n-2}{2}\right) a(n-3)
& \text{if } n \text{ is even} \cr 2 a(n-1) + n a(n-2) & \text{if } n \text{ is odd} \end{cases}$$

*References:*
- [A340737](https://oeis.org/A340737)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
- [b](https://oeis.org/b)
-/

namespace OeisA340737


open MeasureTheory

open scoped Real

open Nat

/--
Numerators of a sequence of fractions converging to $e$.
$$a(1) = 3, a(2) = 5$$
For $n > 2$:
$$a(n) = \begin{cases} \left(\frac{n+2}{2}\right) a(n-1) - a(n-2) -
\left(\frac{n-2}{2}\right) a(n-3)
& \text{if } n \text{ is even} \cr 2 a(n-1) + n a(n-2) & \text{if } n \text{ is odd} \end{cases}$$
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  match n with
  | 0 => 0 -- Required for total function, O(1,1) suggests 0 is not relevant.
  | 1 => 3
  | 2 => 5
  | n' + 3 => -- n $\ge$ 3
    let n := n' + 3

    let a_nm1 := a (n - 1)
    let a_nm2 := a (n - 2)
    let a_nm3 := a (n - 3)

    if n % 2 = 0 then
      -- n is even, n $\ge$ 4
      let c1 : ℕ := (n + 2) / 2
      let c2 : ℕ := (n - 2) / 2

      -- $a(n) = c_1 \cdot a(n-1) - a(n-2) - c_2 \cdot a(n-3)$.
      -- We use Int.ofNat for safe subtraction, as the result is known to be positive.
      Int.toNat (Int.ofNat c1 * Int.ofNat a_nm1 - Int.ofNat a_nm2 - Int.ofNat c2 * Int.ofNat a_nm3)
    else
      -- n is odd, n $\ge$ 3
      2 * a_nm1 + n * a_nm2
termination_by n

/--
Denominators of a sequence of fractions converging to $e$.
This sequence is defined by the same recurrence relation as a but with
initial values $b(1)=1, b(2)=2$.
$$b(1) = 1, b(2) = 2$$
For $n > 2$:
$$b(n) = \begin{cases} \left(\frac{n+2}{2}\right) b(n-1) - b(n-2) -
\left(\frac{n-2}{2}\right) b(n-3)
& \text{if } n \text{ is even} \cr 2 b(n-1) + n b(n-2) & \text{if } n \text{ is odd} \end{cases}$$
-/
def b (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  match n with
  | 0 => 0
  | 1 => 1
  | 2 => 2
  | n' + 3 => -- n $\ge$ 3
    let n := n' + 3

    let b_nm1 := b (n - 1)
    let b_nm2 := b (n - 2)
    let b_nm3 := b (n - 3)

    if n % 2 = 0 then
      -- n is even, n $\ge$ 4
      let c1 : ℕ := (n + 2) / 2
      let c2 : ℕ := (n - 2) / 2

      -- $b(n) = c_1 \cdot b(n-1) - b(n-2) - c_2 \cdot b(n-3)$.
      -- We use Int.ofNat for safe subtraction.
      Int.toNat (Int.ofNat c1 * Int.ofNat b_nm1 - Int.ofNat b_nm2 - Int.ofNat c2 * Int.ofNat b_nm3)
    else
      -- n is odd, n $\ge$ 3
      2 * b_nm1 + n * b_nm2
termination_by n


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 3 := by unfold a; rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 5 := by unfold a; rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 19 := by unfold a; unfold a; unfold a; simp

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 49 := by unfold a; unfold a; unfold a; unfold a; simp

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_5 : a 5 = 193 := by unfold a; unfold a; unfold a; unfold a; unfold a; simp


/--
Conjecture: $\lim_{n \to \infty} a(n) / b(n) = e$, where $b(n)$ is the companion denominator sequence.

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/340737.wip.lean#L438"]
theorem tendsto_exp_one :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (a n : ℝ) / (b n : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (nhds (Real.exp 1)) := by
    sorry

end OeisA340737

findings.description: The module's companion-denominator reference at line 32 is `[b](https://oeis.org/b)`, rather than a reference to OEIS A340738. The definition `OeisA340737.b` is correct; this is only a citation slip.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A340737 explicitly states, "Denominators are listed in A340738." A340738 gives initial values 1, 2 and the same recurrence used by `b`. Read through the official OEIS data mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A340/A340737.seq and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A340/A340738.seq.

reformulations.difference: OEIS starts the fractions at index 1. Lean extends both sequences to index 0 with value 0, so its Nat-indexed quotient includes an initial `0 / 0 = 0`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The added zero values never affect any positive-index term: the recurrence at 3 uses only indices 2 and 1, and the first even recurrence is at 4. Both sequences are positive at every positive index. An initial extra term does not affect convergence atTop. In scratch.lean, I proved both the equivalence with the sequence shifted by one and the equivalence with the epsilon definition requiring a threshold N ≥ 1.

review.notes: All eight declarations were checked; no mathematical misformalization was found. Direct OEIS requests returned Cloudflare 403, so the full entries were read from OEIS's official mirror. Lean computations matched both OEIS sequences through index 16. Independent Lean proofs establish positivity for every positive index and show that Int.toNat never changes the integer recurrence. The solved status agrees with OEIS's June 9, 2026 proof comment and the subsequent cited literature. After updating the external proof's obsolete import and two base-case proof bodies for the current toolchain, proof-transfer.lean proves the exact current limit statement with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. All experiments are in /workspace/review/; the reviewed file is unchanged.
